summary: Entry Certificate backend and desktop UI were exercised end to end. Authenticated/private and public PDF downloads, validation, one-page Letter rendering/branding, token generation/reuse, two successful Resend deliveries, provider rejection mapping, persistence, row/view/email UI actions, toast, Last sent indicator, downloads, login, dashboard, intake, journal CRUD/export, cron auth and Settings alerts all worked. Two regressions were found: ReportLab silently removes angle-bracketed user data from legal certificate fields, and upcoming commission alerts are returned/displayed in reverse chronological order.

critical.issue: User-entered values are passed directly to ReportLab Paragraph and interpreted as markup. Reproduction: signer 'TEST Alice <Signer> & Bob' rendered as 'TEST Alice & Bob', ID 'TEST-<ID>&-0726' rendered as 'TEST-&-0726', and '<script>' tags were stripped. The endpoint returns 200 but silently alters legally significant certificate data.
Static review found signer name, document description, personal note and notary fields interpolated into branded HTML without escaping. Journal/user input can inject arbitrary email HTML and links.

minor.issue: upcoming_alerts is now ordered [0,1,7,14,30], so dates appear latest-to-earliest. The prior chronological contract/test expected [30,14,7,1,0].

integration_issues.issue: The UI faithfully renders the API's [0,1,7,14,30] order, placing expiration day first and the next actual alert last.

action_items: Escape every user-controlled value before passing it to ReportLab Paragraph so literal angle brackets and ampersands are preserved in the certificate.
HTML-escape signer, document, personal-note and notary values in certificate emails; convert note newlines safely rather than interpolating raw HTML.
Sort /api/alerts/status upcoming alerts by alert date (equivalently days_out descending) without changing ascending ALERT_BUCKETS used by bucket selection.

Make certificate-token creation atomic: concurrent first email requests can currently return different tokens because find/update is not conditional; refetch the single winning token after a conditional update.
Retest markup-heavy certificate values, malicious email-note input, and alert ordering after fixes.
critical_code_review_comments: _render_certificate_pdf uses ReportLab's XML-like Paragraph with raw database values; this was reproduced as silent field corruption rather than a visible failure.
email_certificate builds HTML by direct f-string interpolation of stored and request values, enabling HTML injection in recipient emails.

_get_entry_certificate_token performs read-then-unconditional-write despite concurrent email requests; the sparse unique index does not prevent two callers from sending different returned tokens while only the last remains valid.

Certificate links reuse ALERT_APP_URL instead of a certificate/app-base-specific required environment variable, coupling two unrelated features and producing an invalid relative email link if that setting is absent.
server.py is 1,382 lines and mixes auth, alerts, journal, PDF, public links and email rendering; feature-specific escaping and atomicity are harder to enforce in this monolith.

success_rate.backend: 90% unique executed tests (19/21 passed; all requested core certificate cases passed)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of executed Entry Certificate desktop controls/integration and navigation regressions passed

seed_data_creation: Created and deleted one TEST_Certificate UI entry and one markup edge-case entry; intake/journal regression fixtures also cleaned up. Existing certificate metadata and commission state were restored. Five real certificate emails were accepted by Resend across test/retest/UI runs, and one required delivered@resend.dev request was rejected with the surfaced undeliverable message.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Certificate PDF measured 39,594 bytes, one Letter portrait page (612x792), contained required title/type/cert number/date/signer/ID/fee/attestation/commission/footer text, at least one shield image, and verified red/navy drawing colors. Private download returned attachment and 401 without auth; malformed/nonexistent IDs returned 400/404. Public token returned equivalent one-page PDF and bogus token 404. Missing/invalid email returned 422; two sends reused one token and updated recipient/email ID; delivered@resend.dev returned JSON 400 containing 'undeliverable' without overwriting successful metadata. UI create/view/email/download/edit/delete flow passed and temporary entry was deleted. Do not send more real emails unless the developer explicitly resets the volume budget for this iteration.
rca_of_the_issue: Certificate corruption is caused by passing raw user strings into reportlab.platypus.Paragraph, whose mini-HTML parser consumes angle-bracketed text as tags. Email injection has the same missing output-encoding class in the HTML f-string. Alert ordering regressed when ALERT_BUCKETS was corrected to ascending for threshold selection and the status serializer continued iterating that same list; the list now needs an independent chronological sort.
